messages.text: Hi! I watched the videos on your site and heard how loud the boot sequence is. Does that extreme noise happen only on the very first boot out of the box, or every single time the device powers on / reboots? Thanks!

Every power-on, not just the first. The fans spin to full for the first 30 seconds or so while it boots, then settle to a steady hum once it's hashing — that's normal for the 40T.

Where are you thinking of putting it?
why fans spin to full every boot?

It's a self-test. On power-up the controller runs the fans at 100% before it knows the chip temps, then drops them once the firmware takes over thermal control. Standard on ASICs.

At 650 W it's not a bedroom machine either way — garage, basement or office corner is the usual spot. Where would yours sit?
is possible to set it in standby?

You can throttle it down or stop hashing from the miner's web dashboard, and plenty of people put it on a smart plug to schedule off-hours. A true low-power standby mode I don't want to guess at — let me get that confirmed properly rather than make it up.
Handed to the team · Need confirmation on whether the Magic Miner 40T firmware has a standby / idle l

Our hardware guy has it and will jump in right here — stay in the chat and he'll answer, or it comes by email if you step away.

Meanwhile: is noise the main thing you're weighing, or the power draw?
i'll put it in the office but i want to turn off/in standby at the evening and turn on/out standby in the early morning so i want to avoid 30 panic seconds xD

Easy fix: pause hashing in the dashboard instead of cutting power — the unit stays up, so no boot roar when it resumes. If you'd rather use a smart plug, schedule the morning power-on for before you walk in; the 30 loud seconds happen in an empty room.

Office it is. Want me to get one in the cart for you?
i already purchased it. in hashing pause how much it consumes?

I won't guess at that number — paused draw is exactly what I asked our hardware guy, so it's already in his queue with your standby question. He'll answer both right here.

Nice, glad you got one. Ships November 30, 2026.

Checked the live listing. It publishes three running modes — Eco 30 TH/s at 450 W, Standard 40 TH/s at 650 W, Turbo 850 W (overclock, voids warranty) — and no figure for paused or idle. So I'd be making it up; that one stays with our hardware guy.

One real option for your evenings: drop it to Eco. Quieter, ~50 dB, and still hashing.
i need to know how much is the consumption in standby mode so with hashing in pause thx

Understood — that exact number is what's sitting with our hardware guy, and it's the only way you'll get a figure that's real rather than a guess. He's on today and will post it right here; if you step away it comes by email.
